RPE Scale (Rate of Perceived Exertion)
Based on Reps in Reserve (RIR):

  • 10 - Max effort, could not do another rep
  • 9.5 - Could maybe do 1 more rep
  • 9 - Could definitely do 1 more rep
  • 8 - Could do 2 more reps
  • 7 - Could do 3 more reps
  • 6 - Could do 4+ reps
  • For strength (heavy): aim for RPE 7.5-8.5
  • For volume (light): aim for RPE 7-8

Weighted Linear Regression with Exponential Decay
• Heavy workouts: Always included\n• Light workouts: Only with RPE data\n• Prevents skewing the strength curve
• With RPE: Effective reps = actual + RIR\n• Example: 100kg × 5 reps @ RPE 8 = 7 effective reps\n• No RPE: Assumes near failure
• Sets with RPE < 6.5 are excluded\n• Ensures only challenging sets are used
• ≤8 reps: Epley\'s formula\n• 9-15 reps: Brzycki\'s formula\n• >15 reps: Discarded
• Recent sessions have more influence\n• Exponential decay: λ = 0.02 (~35 day half-life)\n• Adapts quickly to current trends
• Applies Law of Diminishing Returns\n• 1 month: 100%, 2 months: 90%\n• 3 months: 80%, 6 months: 50%
Realistic and scientifically accurate progress predictions based on maximal effort sessions.

Suggested RPE values:
• Strength: Novice 8.0, Intermediate 8.5
• Build: Novice 7.5, Intermediate 8.0
• Flush: Novice 7.0, Intermediate 7.5

1. Start with base rest time (Heavy/Light/Custom)
2. If RPE ≥ High Threshold: +Bonus seconds
3. If logged RPE ≥ suggested+threshold: +Positive adjustment
4. If logged RPE ≤ suggested-threshold: -Negative adjustment
Example: Strength intent, Intermediate, logged RPE 9.5\nBase: 180s + High RPE bonus (9.5≥9.0): +60s + Deviation (9.5-8.5=1.0): +30s = 270s total
